Labour Code 45/2019/QH14 art.113(1)(a): 12 working days in normal conditions; art.113(2) with Decree 145/2020/ND-CP art.66(1): under twelve months, the share of the months worked in the year; art.114: one more day for every full five years with the employer. art.113(1)(b)–(c) set 14 and 16 days for minors, workers with disabilities and arduous, toxic or dangerous work. art.113(4): leave is combined over at most three years only by agreement.

Law on Social Insurance 2024 art.43(1)(b): the longer bands are for work that is arduous, toxic or dangerous, or especially so (`classification in [ARDUOUS, ESPECIALLY_ARDUOUS]`).

references.title: Labour Code 2019 art.139(1) with Law on Social Insurance 41/2024/QH15 art.53 — six months before and after childbirth, one further month for each child from the second in a multiple birth, paid from the social insurance fund at 100% of the average contribution salary of the six months before the leave. six months per birth, one more for every further child of a multiple birth (art.139(1); one further month read for a twin or more), seven months from 1 July 2026 only where the mother had exactly one living biological child at this birth (Population Law 113/2025 art.14(1)(a), Decree 168/2026 art.2(1)(a); `children.natural_surviving_before(event.date) == 1`; complete dated child history is required), for a member of six months’ contributions in the twelve before the birth (Law 41/2024 art.50; `SI.since_months`); paid by the fund at the six-month average, not by the employer (`paid_by: FUND`). Labour Code 2019 art.139: every female employee has the six months’ leave; the allowance is the fund’s (`paid_by: FUND`) and needs six months of contributions in the twelve before the birth (Law on Social Insurance 2024 art.50) — a mother short of it is on leave without the allowance, not without the leave. the grant is calendar months, not days (`calendar_months`): Labour Code 2019 art.139(1) “06 tháng … thêm 01 tháng” for each child from the second of a multiple birth (triplets eight months, `children.born_on(event.date)`), counted from the event’s first leave day, rest days and holidays inside the period (Law 41/2024 art.53(9)); the law states no day arithmetic, so the period ends the day before the same day of the closing month, or on that month’s last day where it has none (recorded default). Engine (round 7): calendar days of six months from the first leave day, one month more per further child of the birth, seven months for a second child (entry fact second_child: the mother had exactly one living biological child) (entry facts event_id, children_born); an adoption runs to the child's six months (Law 41/2024 art.56); a man takes it for an adoption, after the mother's death or as the commissioning father (Law 41/2024 arts.53, 56–57; entry fact maternity_case). A second-child birth of twins or more adds the multiple-birth month on top of the seven: Labour Code art.139(1) as amended by Population Law 113/2025/QH15 art.29(1) (“sinh đôi trở lên thì tính từ con thứ hai trở đi, cứ mỗi con, người mẹ được nghỉ thêm 01 tháng”), eight months for second-child twins (Ministry of Home Affairs answer, https://lsvn.vn/bo-noi-vu-giai-dap-ve-truong-hop-duoc-nghi-thai-san-8-thang-a178778.html).

Law on Social Insurance 41/2024/QH15 art.53(2) — five working days for an insured father, seven where the birth is by caesarean section or before 32 weeks, ten for twins with three more for each further child, and fourteen for twins delivered by caesarean section; the leave must fall within 60 days of the birth. five working days per birth, seven for a caesarean or a birth before 32 weeks, ten for twins and fourteen for twins by caesarean (Law 41/2024 art.53(2); `event.kind`); paid by the fund (`paid_by: FUND`). From 1 July 2026, Decree 168/2026/NĐ-CP art.2(1)(b) grants ten working days for a second child where the wife had exactly one prior living biological child; the wife’s event-specific count is required for single births, while multiple-birth grants remain higher. Official Gazette.

Law 41/2024 art.53(3), effective 1 July 2025. Every paternity segment must START within the first 60 calendar days, counting the birth/event day as day 1; it may finish later. Exact official BHXH HCMC example published 10 February 2026: birth 10 September 2025 permits starts through 8 November inclusive; 9 November is too late.
